author: robzilla79
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a single authoritative, deterministic reference for the kernel governance lifecycle and how runtime stages map to artifact production and state transitions.
- Make explicit the expected per-stage artifacts, system state updates, common failure modes, and which tests are typically impacted to improve operability and reduce ambiguity.
- Record the canonical `run_result.json` layout, final artifact directory layout under `output/runs/<run_id>/`, and immutable exit code semantics for automation consumers.

### Description
- Add `truth/KERNEL_EXECUTION_PIPELINE.md` documenting the governance-ordered stages `RESEARCH → PLAN → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → PUBLISH` and noting internal runtime stages grouped under PLAN/IMPLEMENT.
- For each governance stage the document lists Purpose, Artifacts produced, System state updates, Common failure modes, and Tests typically affected.
- Document the deterministic final artifact layout under `output/runs/<run_id>/`, provide the `run_result.json` structure and deterministic serialization requirements, and state exit code semantics (`0`, `1`, `2`).
- Emphasize determinism-related expectations (sorted artifact lists, SHA256 manifests, and no timestamp/non-deterministic serialization) for downstream tooling and proof bundles.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed because this is a documentation-only change; no code behavior was modified.

author: dylanscott
body:
This PR refactors the `check` and `run` commands per the discussion in #114. In summary:

- `check` just checks diagnostics, and can be scoped either to a markdown file or a GSQL file
- Taking screenshots is now handled by the `run` command, including the `--chart` flag. Additionally, a `--query` flag can be used to run a code-fenced query from a markdown file.
- **Note**: Contra what was said in #114 I decided _not_ to support `graphene run [ gsqlFile ]`. My reasoning is that it feels counter to the goal of the original issue: The agent should not be iterating on a GSQL query in a separate scratch file, which has the same drift problems. It should ideally iterate on queries in the markdown file/code fence.

Fixes #114.

author: fudoniten
body:
## Summary
Added a custom JSON encoder for `java.time.Duration` objects to serialize them as human-readable time strings in HH:MM:SS format.

## Changes
- Registered a new Jackson JSON encoder for `java.time.Duration` type
- Converts duration values to formatted time strings (hours:minutes:seconds)
- Uses zero-padded two-digit format for each time component

## Implementation Details
The encoder extracts the total seconds from the duration and calculates:
- Hours: total seconds divided by 3600
- Minutes: remaining seconds after hours, divided by 60
- Seconds: final remainder after minutes

The result is formatted as a string with the pattern `%02d:%02d:%02d` to ensure consistent two-digit representation of each component.

author: sambarker
body:
Jekyll posts have a date. Jekyll has a configurable behaviour about whether to include future dated posts, which defaults to [false](https://github.com/jekyll/jekyll/blob/d0cf1791f6a349519998750f4511822e43e516e4/lib/jekyll/configuration.rb#L31). This means future-dated posts are excluded during static generation. Our site builds are only driven by merging PRs to this repository. So if we accidentally future-date a Release Blog, then it can happen that on merge it is not made visible and will not be until another PR is merged after the post date. This is not what we are intending when we hit the Merge button.

This PR adds a couple of checks. 

1. To catch PRs where the front matter is older than the filename. likely to be a mistake. 
2. To add a warning on merge when future dated posts are merged  as they require manual publishing. Example https://github.com/SamBarker/kroxylicious.github.io/actions/runs/22653880628

author: domenic
body:
As discussed in https://github.com/jsdom/cssstyle/issues/318, over time cssstyle has become increasingly coupled with the internals of jsdom. Ongoing work on improving style resolution, and future work on moving `CSSStyleDeclaration` to webidl2js, will only increase this coupling. As such, we merge the cssstyle package into jsdom.

Doing so while using `@acemir/cssom` directly is difficult, since `@acemir/cssom` hard-codes the `cssstyle` package name, and won't properly integrate with a jsdom-internal `CSSStyleDeclaration`. Additionaly, `@acemir/cssom` is a package with a lot of historical baggage, including a custom build system, its own parser, an ES5-era codebase, and various nonstandard extensions. As such, this includes fresh reimplementations of all of the CSSOM classes, using webidl2js wrappers, and using the csstree parser instead of a custom parser, with extra work to match the latest specs (or document deviations from them).

Some specific improvements over `@acemir/cssom`:

* `CSSMediaRule`/`CSSSupportsRule` `matches` getters
* Proper media query parsing in `MediaList` (instead of just splitting on commas)
* `CSSKeyframeRule` `keyText` getter/setter with validation
* `CSSStyleRule` `selectorText` setter rejects invalid selectors
* `CSSStyleSheet` `replace()` properly defers to a microtask, and the "disallow modification flag" is checked in all methods.
* `StyleSheet` `ownerNode`, `href`, and `title` are set.
* No nonstandard extensions (e.g. `CSSDocumentRule`, `CSSHostRule`, `CSSValue`, `MatcherList`, various parser-related methods).

Fixes #690. Fixes #992. Fixes #2974. Fixes #3766. Fixes #3988.
 
This is not perfect. In particular, csstree does not have a spec-compliant serializer, and its parser needs some hacks to be spec-compliant. (See https://github.com/csstree/csstree/issues/52 and the `css-parser.js` file.) So the ideal strategy, of parsing, storing AST notes, and serializing, is not possible. Instead, we do our best to preserve the input as strings, and serialize it back out; this gives reasonable results (at least as good as `@acemir/cssom`). In the future it may be worth investigating other CSS parsers like PostCSS, `@adobe/css-tools`, or similar. For now, since cssstyle was using csstree, we do so in jsdom.

As part of this work, consolidate all CSS-related files into `lib/jsdom/living/css/`, moving several from `lib/jsdom/living/helpers/`. Many of the files from cssstyle were also renamed as part of the merge.

Many new to-upstream web platform tests are included, on an ad-hoc basis: they test things that came up in earlier drafts of this work, and are not an exhaustive test of all CSSOM functionality.

Note that apart from renames, the imported cssstyle code is mostly unchanged; in particular, `CSSStyleDeclaration` is still not using webidl2js.

body:
## Summary

Fixes #264 — notifications are unreliable: mention badges missing, push inconsistent, @channel/@here broken in public channels.

**7 bugs fixed:**

- **`desktopEnabled: false` blocked ALL notification records** — removed from `shouldNotify()` since it's a client-side display concern. Bell badges, push, and mention counts now always work regardless of desktop toggle.
- **@channel/@here broken for public channels** — was querying `channelMembership` (only populated for private channels). Now uses community `membership` for public channels.
- **DM group members silenced when message has @mentions** — mentioning 1 user in a 4-person DM no longer skips the other 2. `createDMNotifications()` now filters out already-notified users instead of being skipped entirely.
- **Thread notifications suppressed by channel mute** — `THREAD_REPLY` now bypasses channel override check (explicit subscription = explicit opt-in).
- **CHANNEL_MESSAGE notifications never created** — new `createChannelMessageNotifications()` method creates records for users with "All Messages" level. 500-member safety threshold for public channels.
- **`markContextNotificationsAsRead` incomplete** — added `CHANNEL_MESSAGE` to the channel types list so auto-clearing works after bug 5 fix.
- **No window focus / active channel suppression** — new `useWindowFocus` hook + path-based check suppresses sounds and desktop notifications when actively viewing the same channel/DM.

Also adds `THREAD_REPLY` to the shared `NotificationType` enum and `NOTIFICATION_SOUND_MAP`.

author: kerneldeimos
body: It turns out there are nuances between `puter.ui.authenticateWithPuter` vs `puter.auth.signIn` - these don't do the same thing. The primary difference is that `puter.ui.authenticateWithPuter` will display an override if it's not triggered by a user action, whereas `puter.auth.signIn` will not. This definitely suggests `puter.ui.authenticateWithPuter` should be a caller of `puter.auth.signIn` instead of implementing its own logic for handling the popup - that makes this part of the code more fagile - but that refactor is out-of-scope for this bug fix.

body:
## Summary
- Tightened agent usage instructions to enforce gateway-only Chrome interaction through the relay.
- Required tab-scoped execution (`--tab-id`) for all autonomous runs to reduce random tab/profile takeover risk.
- Added explicit stop conditions when the requested tab is not attached in relay status.

## Why this change
- Current behavior reports showed agents sometimes acting on unintended Chrome contexts.
- Immediate mitigation is to harden operational instructions so agents never run unscoped browser control flows.

## What changed
- `SKILL.md`

  - Explicitly prohibited direct browser automation tools for this workflow.
  - Required `--tab-id` for all agent runs (single and concurrent).
  - Added guard to stop when requested `tabId` is absent from `attachedTabs`.
  - Clarified that unscoped command examples are manual/debug-only.
- `AGENTS.md`
  - Added matching gateway-only and no-direct-control contract language.
  - Enforced `--tab-id` for all agent reads/checks.
  - Added explicit re-attach gate when `tabId` is missing from attached tabs.
  - Added safety note in workflow section that autonomous runs must be tab-scoped.

## Files changed

- `SKILL.md`

- Behavioral impact: stricter instructions may require users/agents to supply `--tab-id` consistently.

## Summary

Two major features inspired by PicoClaw research:

### 1. System Prompt Caching
- Intelligent caching of static system prompt with mtime-based invalidation
- Reduces redundant file I/O on every message
- Tracks: AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, USER.md, TOOLS.md, IDENTITY.md, MEMORY.md, skills/*/SKILL.md
- Thread-safe with double-checked locking pattern
- `InvalidatePromptCache()` for force refresh

### 2. Model-Centric Configuration
- Simplified model configuration with provider auto-detection
- Fallback chain support for resilience
- Environment variable overrides (`JOSHBOT_MODELS_CONFIG__*`)
- Backward compatible with legacy `providers` config
- Provider detection for 9 providers: anthropic, openai, groq, ollama, openrouter, nvidia, deepseek, gemini, cerebras

```json
{
  "models_config": {
    "models": [

      {"name": "fast", "model": "groq/llama-3.3-70b", "api_key": "..."}
    ],
    "agent": {"model": "smart", "fallback": ["fast"]}

}

```bash
JOSHBOT_MODELS_CONFIG__MODELS__0__NAME=openrouter

body:
### Motivation
- Two unit tests were failing: the streaming urgent dispatch ordering test and the GPU fluid settling test, indicating urgent generation jobs were not re-queued with the right priority and liquid voxels could drift laterally across chunk boundaries instead of settling.
- The change aims to preserve urgent-job priority when dispatch is deferred and prevent lateral liquid moves when a voxel is already supported by adjacent liquid so settling remains contiguous across chunk boundaries.

### Description
- Change `defer_generation_dispatch` in `src/streaming.rs` to reinsert deferred `GenerateJobClass::Urgent` jobs at the front of `pending_generate` and preserve queue metadata by updating `enqueue_seq` and `generate_meta` accordingly.
- Keep background (non-urgent) deferrals using the existing `enqueue_generate` path so they remain appended to the queue.
- In `src/simulation/gpu_fluid.rs`, add a guard in `advect_material_states` to skip same-level lateral moves for `Phase::Liquid` when the source voxel already has adjacent liquid neighbors.
- Add a `has_adjacent_liquid` helper that checks the four lateral neighbors in the snapshot and uses `material(...).phase` to detect adjacent liquid.

### Testing
- Ran `cargo test --lib streaming::tests::deferred_urgent_dispatch_stays_queued_at_front -- --exact` and the test passed.
- Ran `cargo test --lib simulation::gpu_fluid::tests::liquid_settles_continuously_across_boundary -- --exact` and the test passed.
- Ran full library test suite with `cargo test --lib` and all tests passed (`53 passed; 0 failed`).

### Motivation

- Ensure encryption state is determined from the actual database (meta.json / file contents) instead of relying solely on possibly-stale preferences. 
- Persist a canonical `encrypted` flag to `meta.json` so the app can recover and report correct encryption state across restarts and when `safeStorage` is unavailable.
- Reduce duplicated meta.json read/write logic and make updates more robust with centralized error handling.

### Description

- Added `hasEncryptedDataInDatabase()` to detect whether the current database contains encrypted data by preferring `meta.json.encrypted` and falling back to scanning `objects` and `trash` files for `ENCRYPTED:` markers.
- Introduced `updateMetaJson(databaseDir, updater, options)` helper that centralizes reading, mutating, and writing `meta.json` with consistent error logging.
- Changed the `encryption:is-enabled` IPC handler to compute the enabled state using `hasEncryptedDataInDatabase()` instead of reading preferences.
- Updated flows to keep `meta.json.encrypted` in sync: `generate-recovery-key` now sets `encrypted = true` and saves `databasePath`, `encryption:disable` sets `encrypted = false`, and batch `encrypt-all` / `decrypt-all` use `updateMetaJson` to flip the flag; added corresponding logs and defensive JSON parsing.

### Testing

author: copilot
body:
Implements YOLO11 object tracking on an RTSP input stream, with simultaneous local display and annotated RTSP output via FFmpeg — following the [Ultralytics tracking docs](https://docs.ultralytics.com/modes/track/).

## Core script — `rtsp_track.py`

Uses `model.track()` in streaming/persistent mode with a configurable tracker YAML:

```python
results = model.track(
    source=args.source,
    tracker=args.tracker,   # botsort.yaml / bytetrack.yaml / custom_tracker.yaml
    persist=True,           # maintain track IDs across frames
    stream=True,            # memory-efficient generator
    conf=args.conf,
    iou=args.iou,
)
for result in results:
    frame = result.plot()
    cv2.imshow("YOLO11 RTSP Tracking", frame)          # local display
    ffmpeg_proc.stdin.write(frame.tobytes())            # → RTSP output
```

FFmpeg receives raw BGR frames via stdin and pushes H.264 to the output RTSP server (`libx264 -preset ultrafast -tune zerolatency`).

## Tracker config — `custom_tracker.yaml`

BoT-SORT config with all knobs exposed and documented. Switch algorithm via `tracker_type: botsort | bytetrack`. Key settings:

- `gmc_method: sparseOptFlow` — global motion compensation for moving cameras
- `with_reid: false` — ReID off by default; toggle with model path via `model:`

## Notable design decisions

- **Credentials via env var**: `RTSP_SOURCE` env var overrides the default source URL; avoids embedding credentials in CLI history or source.
- **`--tracker`** accepts any YAML path, enabling per-deployment tracker tuning without code changes.
- **FFmpeg optional**: if `ffmpeg` is not on `PATH`, output is gracefully disabled with a warning; local display still works.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide per-tick observability for core loop determinism by recording a compact tick log containing session, tick, loop/state transition, interventions, selected action, seed and error codes. 
- Consolidate decision-related outputs (neuron decisions, job selection, intervention results, state transitions) into a single collector to enable log-based replay verification and easier debugging. 
- Implement an automated check for deterministic replay (T23) that flags core-field mismatches with a clear error code (`E-RPL-001`).

### Description
- Added tick log models in `Assets/Scripts/IngameCore/Simulation/TickLogModels.cs` defining `TickLogRecord`, `DecisionTraceLog` and `ReplayVerificationResult` with the requested core and decision-trace fields. 
- Implemented `EventLogCollector` in `Assets/Scripts/IngameCore/Simulation/EventLogCollector.cs` to collect per-tick `BeginTick`/`EndTick`, `RecordStateTransition`, `RecordInterventionResult`, `RecordNeuronDecision` and `RecordJobDecision`, and added a `ReplayVerifier` that compares core fields and emits `E-RPL-001` on mismatch. 
- Extended `JobSystem` (`Assets/Scripts/IngameCore/Simulation/JobSystem.cs`) with `JobDecisionTrace`, a scored candidate list and an overload `AssignBestJob(..., out JobDecisionTrace)` that populates `decision_trace_id`, `candidate_actions`, `candidate_scores`, `blocked_actions` and `selected_action_id`. 
- Wired logging into runtime paths by updating `SimulationTickEngine` (`Assets/Scripts/IngameCore/Simulation/SimulationTickEngine.cs`) to accept an optional `EventLogCollector`, emit `BeginTick`/`EndTick`, record job traces and a basic state transition, and by passing the collector into `CharacterNeuronSystem`. 
- Made `CharacterNeuronSystem` optionally accept the collector and record neuron decisions from `EvaluateCore` so neuron decisions are included in the tick trace. 
- Added two edit-mode tests in `Assets/Tests/EditMode/IngameCoreSimulationTests.cs` to assert deterministic replay logs match for identical seed+input and that `ReplayVerifier` records `E-RPL-001` on core-field mismatch.

### Testing
- Added unit tests `T23_DeterministicReplay_LogCoreFieldsMatchForSameSeedAndInput` and `ReplayVerifier_RecordsERPL001OnCoreFieldMismatch` under `Assets/Tests/EditMode/IngameCoreSimulationTests.cs` but no Unity test runner was executed in this environment. 
- Performed local repository checks including staging and commit which succeeded (changes committed). 
- Static/manual validation performed by inspecting modified files and confirming `EventLogCollector` is invoked from `SimulationTickEngine` and that `JobDecisionTrace` and `ReplayVerifier` are present and used; no automated Unity test run was available in this CI-less environment.

author: joerobich
body:
## Ship Roslyn analyzers (BannedApi, PublicApi, PerformanceSensitive, ResxSourceGenerator) in the SDK

This change bundles four additional Roslyn analyzer packages into the SDK layout, following the same pattern used for CodeStyle and NetAnalyzers today:

- **Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.BannedApiAnalyzers**
- **Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.PublicApiAnalyzers**
- **Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.PerformanceSensitiveAnalyzers**
- **Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.ResxSourceGenerator**

### Opt-in properties

All four are **opt-in** (default `false`). Users enable them by setting the corresponding MSBuild property:

| Property | Analyzer |
|----------|----------|
| `EnableBannedApiAnalysis` | BannedApiAnalyzers |
| `EnablePublicApiAnalysis` | PublicApiAnalyzers |
| `EnablePerformanceSensitiveAnalysis` | PerformanceSensitiveAnalyzers |
| `EnableResxSourceGeneration` | ResxSourceGenerator |

### NuGet package dedup

When a project also references one of these packages directly via NuGet, the SDK-bundled copy is automatically removed to avoid duplicate diagnostics. This is handled entirely on the SDK side (via the `_ResolveSdkAnalyzerConflicts` target) so that it works correctly even against older NuGet package versions that have no awareness of the SDK-bundled analyzers.

### What changed

- **`redist.csproj`** — Added `PackageReference` entries (with `ExcludeAssets="All" GeneratePathProperty="true"`) so the packages are downloaded for layout extraction.
- **`GenerateLayout.targets`** — Extended `PublishNETAnalyzers` to copy analyzer DLLs and build assets into `roslynanalyzers/` subdirectories of the SDK layout.
- **`Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Analyzers.targets`** — Added Enable\* property defaults, `<Import>` of each package's `.props`/`.targets`, `<Analyzer>` item groups gated on the Enable\* properties, and the `_ResolveSdkAnalyzerConflicts` dedup target.
- **`Version.Details.xml` / `Version.Details.props` / `Directory.Packages.props`** — Added version entries for the three new packages (PublicApiAnalyzers already existed).

author: leochiu-a
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

body: Add new functions to allow customizing the mouse cursor's appearance and behavior. No default behaviors should be changed. - Add MouseRenderer::setSpriteSize(), setSpriteColor(), and setClickPoint() to allow customizing the mouse cursor sprite. - Add convenience functions setClickPointCenter() and setClickPointTopLeft() to position the click point to the sprite center (default behavior) or the top-left corner. - Add drawLine visualization on Debug builds to show the sprite bounds and click point. For example, the default EE mouse cursor is a 32x32 pixel image, in which the cursor occupies the bottom-right quarter and the click point is at the image's center point. To use a 16x16 pixel image with the click pointat the top left: ``` mouse_renderer->setSpriteImage("mouse_16.png"); mouse_renderer->setSpriteSize(16.0f); mouse_renderer->setClickPointTopLeft(); ```

author: mattwellie
body:
# Purpose

  - VDS -> MT densification is currently pretty rubbish

## Issues

This process walks a dataset from sparse VDS to dense MT in a few steps. Mixed in is the use of `default_compute_info`, which uses the gVCF_info data to generate pseudo-annotations, as if the data were freshly joint called. 

  - The original implementation here _worked_, but not well. It delegates most of the local-to-global attribute changes to `hl.experimental`, which doesn't correctly update all the fields. E.g. PL might currently be wrongly formatted in our MatrixTables
  - There are a couple of blessed Hail methods `hl.vds.local_to_global` and `hl.vds.lgt_to_gt` which should have been used, but I wasn't aware of them at the time
  - We split multiallelic variants out onto separate rows, but because not all annotations were correctly swapped from global to local (e.g. LPL instead of PL), this was done using `hl.experimental.sparse_split_multi(mt)`, which doesn't split all fields correctly. 

## Re-Write

This process has been redrafted to include a few changes

  - initial densification is unchanged, with the gvcf info fields still generated and annotated in as before
  - LGT, LPL, and LAD fields are all decoded to the global annotation using specific methods, including `mt.LA` to decode the fields.
  - After the entries are updated, the MT is split using the proper method, which should result in accurate splitting of all relevant fields (GT, AD, PL) into separate variants in the final MT. 

## Testing

I've tested the syntax on some PopGen test VDS-format data, but that data did not include multiallelic variants. It would be good to run this in test on some VDS data

## Checklist

- [x] Version Bump!
- [ ] Related GitHub Issue created
- [ ] Tests covering new change
- [ ] Linting checks pass

---

Other issues from hail source code/docstring
**VCF Info Fields**

Hail does not split fields in the info field. This means that if a
multiallelic site with `info.AC` value ``[10, 2]`` is split, each split
site will contain the same array ``[10, 2]``. The provided allele index
field `a_index` can be used to select the value corresponding to the split
allele's position:

```
>>> split_ds = hl.split_multi_hts(dataset)
>>> split_ds = split_ds.filter_rows(split_ds.info.AC[split_ds.a_index - 1] < 10, keep = False)
```

solution = reduce the AC value back down to 1 in the final output
```
>>> split_ds = hl.split_multi_hts(dataset)
>>> split_ds = split_ds.annotate_rows(info = split_ds.info.annotate(AC = split_ds.info.AC[split_ds.a_index - 1]))
>>> hl.export_vcf(split_ds, 'output/export.vcf')
```

At this stage we should also run a minrep call post splitting, to normalise the ref and alt alleles. This will aid in annotation with downstream resources (VEP, AVI, etc.)
https://hail.is/docs/0.2/functions/genetics.html#hail.expr.functions.min_rep

* what happens if/when a non-normalised variant is normalised? Do we end up with 2 competing variants with the same minimally represented CHR-POS-REF-ALT? 
* If we do end up with doubles in the dataset, does each have variant calls attributed to different samples?

use a tool de banco de dados para pesquisar as informações necessárias

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a device-focused WinForms demo that talks to Opta over a TCP text command channel instead of directly using Modbus on port 502. 
- Present a unified UI for AI4/DO8/DIO4/DI8 with clear AI4 differential vs single-ended display rules and per-channel controls. 
- Implement a reliable polling/command queue so `SET` commands are serialized with periodic `READ` polling and Opta IO is throttled to avoid bursts.

### Description
- Implement a full UI and runtime in `Form1.cs` including tabbed device views (AI4/DO8/DIO4/DI8), a right-side console with command input, and per-channel controls and editors. 
- Add a TCP client-based Opta communication layer targeting `192.168.2.100:5000` with throttling (`OptaIoIntervalMs`), a polling timer, a `ConcurrentQueue` for queued `SET` commands, and parsing helpers (`TryExtractType`, `TryExtractLastInt`, `TryExtractOnOff`, etc.).

## Summary

Enterprise governance framework, shared workflow store, and dynamic model metadata — a complete set of features for team/org-level control over JD.AI behavior.

### Governance & Policy Engine
- **Policy engine** with YAML-based policy documents at global, org, project scope
- **Tool restrictions** — allow/deny lists with glob matching (ReDoS-protected)

- **Budget tracking** — persistent daily/monthly spend limits with file-backed storage

- **Data redaction** — regex-based PII/secret scrubbing engine

### Shared Workflow Store
- **IWorkflowStore** interface with Publish, Get, Catalog, Search, Versions, Install

### Organization Instructions

### Dynamic Model Metadata (LiteLLM)
- **ModelMetadataProvider** fetches from LiteLLM catalog, caches with 12h TTL (gzip)
- **ModelIdMatcher** — 4-tier matching (exact, provider-prefixed, bare suffix, normalized stem)

### System Prompt Budget

- **Workflow store wired**: JDAI_WORKFLOW_STORE_URL env var, local fallback

author: chubes4
body:
## Summary

Three fixes for the WordPress extension test infrastructure:

**1. SQLite drop-in: override `db_connect()`**
`WP_UnitTestCase::set_up()` calls `$wpdb->db_connect()` on every test (line 69 of `abstract-testcase.php`). Without the override, the parent `wpdb::db_connect()` tries to open a MySQL socket connection → fails with "No such file or directory" → calls `wp_die()`. This was causing **161+ test errors** across all projects using SQLite mode.

**2. SQLite drop-in: translate MySQL transaction/session commands**
`WP_UnitTestCase` uses `SET autocommit = 0` and `START TRANSACTION` for test isolation — both are MySQL-only syntax that SQLite rejects. Also handles `SET storage_engine`, `SHOW`, `DESCRIBE`, `SET NAMES`, etc.

**3. Bundle `wp-cli/wp-cli` as dev dependency**
Any WordPress plugin with CLI commands extends `WP_CLI_Command`. Without this package in the test environment, PHPUnit gets `Class "WP_CLI_Command" not found` when loading test files that reference CLI command classes.

## Impact

Unblocks SQLite-backed tests for all projects using `homeboy-action`. Previously, every `WP_UnitTestCase` test that touched the database would fail with `WPDieException: Error establishing a database connection`.

author: copilot
body:
面向国内封锁网络的完整开发环境管理方案：GitHub Actions 手动触发构建 amd64 镜像 → GHCR → 阿里云OSS/华为OBS → 目标机离线 `docker load`，全程无需目标机访问外网。

**当前阶段**：仅支持 `linux/amd64`（x86_64）。arm64 为可选未来计划，待 amd64 验证稳定后手动扩展。

## 分层镜像体系

- **L0** `base/` — Ubuntu 22.04 amd64（APT 替换为阿里云镜像源）+ openEuler 22.03 LTS amd64（华为云镜像源，替代麒麟，无授权问题）
- **L1** `toolchain/` — GCC14/Clang18/CMake/Ninja、Google Benchmark 1.8.3、Python 3.12+uv、zsh/tmux/vim/SSH
- **L2** `services/` — Docker CE + Podman + nerdctl、Ansible 9.3 + 常用 Collection
- **L3** `compose/` — `full`/`cpp`/`python` 三种场景组合镜像，含项目模板文件

## CI/CD 流水线（5 个 Workflow，全部手动触发）

所有 Workflow 均通过 `workflow_dispatch` 手动触发，不含任何自动触发事件（无 `push`、`schedule`、`workflow_run`、`release`）。所有 Workflow 配置并发控制（`concurrency`），以 `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` 为 group，不同分支可并行运行，同一分支新任务触发时自动取消旧任务（`cancel-in-progress: true`）。

- `build-matrix.yml` — 手动选层构建（base/toolchain/services/compose/all），`linux/amd64` 单架构
- `push-registry.yml` — 手动触发通过 `skopeo` 推送到阿里云ACR / 华为SWR，VERSION 默认回退到 `latest`
- `sync-oss.yml` / `sync-obs.yml` — 手动触发将镜像导出为 `.tar.zst` 上传对象存储，默认架构 amd64，可选 arm64/both，VERSION 默认回退到 `latest`
- `auto-update.yml` — 手动触发全量重建（已移除月度 cron）

## 目标机分发与初始化

```bash
# 一键初始化（自动检测架构、安装运行时、从OSS拉取镜像）
./scripts/bootstrap.sh --scene full --registry oss

# 初始化后启动开发容器
devenv /path/to/src
```

`distribution/loader/load.sh` 支持 OSS/OBS/HTTP 三种分发源，下载后 SHA256 校验，支持断点续传。

## Ansible 批量运维

四个 Playbook：`bootstrap.yml`（初始化运行时）、`deploy-env.yml`（部署）、`update-env.yml`（检查版本差异按需更新）、`health-check.yml`。

## 统一 Makefile 入口

```makefile
make build LAYER=toolchain          # 分层构建
make build IMAGE=cpp                # 单镜像构建（amd64）
make push-all-registries            # 推送所有仓库
make sync TARGET=all                # 同步 OSS + OBS
make ansible-deploy SCENE=cpp       # Ansible 批量部署
```

所有配置集中在 `config/matrix.yaml`（构建矩阵 DAG，仅 amd64）、`config/registry.yaml`、`config/mirror.yaml`（含 openEuler yum 源）；敏感值全部通过 GitHub Secrets / 环境变量注入。

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

# 开发环境一体化方案大纲

## 总体架构

```
GitHub (源码 / Actions / Copilot / Packages)
         ↓
   分层镜像构建体系 (BuildKit + QEMU 多架构)
         ↓
    GHCR → 阿里云OSS / 华为OBS（对象存储分发）
         ↓
目标环境（Ubuntu x86_64 / 麒麟 ARM64）
         ↓
   本地 Docker / Podman / containerd 运行时
```

---

## 一、项目结构设计

```
devenv/
├── .github/
│   ├── workflows/
│   │   ├── build-matrix.yml       # 全量/分层构建
│   │   ├── push-registry.yml      # 推送镜像仓库
│   │   ├── sync-oss.yml           # 同步到阿里云OSS
│   │   ├── sync-obs.yml           # 同步到华为OBS
│   │   └── auto-update.yml        # 定时自动维护
│   └── copilot-instructions.md    # Copilot 上下文定制
│
├── base/                          # L0：基础系统层
│   ├── ubuntu-amd64/
│   ├── ubuntu-arm64/
│   └── kylin-arm64/
│
├── toolchain/                     # L1：语言与工具链层
│   ├── cpp/                       # GCC/Clang/CMake
│   ├── gbench/                    # Google Benchmark
│   ├── python/                    # Python + uv/pip
│   └── common/                    # Git/zsh/tmux/vim
│
├── services/                      # L2：可选服务层
│   ├── docker/                    # Docker-in-Docker / Podman
│   └── ansible/                   # Ansible + 常用 Collection
│
├── compose/                       # L3：场景组合层
│   ├── dev-full/
│   ├── dev-cpp/
│   └── dev-python/
│
├── distribution/                  # 分发管理
│   ├── oss/                       # 阿里云OSS脚本
│   ├── obs/                       # 华为OBS脚本
│   └── loader/                    # 目标机拉取/加载脚本
│
├── ansible/                       # 自动化运维
│   ├── playbooks/
│   │   ├── bootstrap.yml          # 初始化目标机
│   │   ├── deploy-env.yml         # 部署开发环境
│   │   └── update-env.yml         # 更新维护
│   └── inventory/
│
├── scripts/
│   ├── build.sh                   # 构建统一入口
│   ├── push.sh                    # 推送统一入口
│   ├── sync.sh                    # OSS/OBS同步入口
│   ├── load.sh                    # 目标机一键加载
│   └── bootstrap.sh               # 目标机一键初始化
│
├── config/
│   ├── matrix.yaml                # 构建矩阵定义
│   ├── registry.yaml              # 镜像仓库配置
│   └── mirror.yaml                # 国内镜像源配置
│
└── Makefile                       # 顶层统一入口
```

---

## 二、分层镜像体系

| 层级 | 镜像名 | 核心内容 | 架构 | 重建频率 |
|------|--------|----------|------|----------|
| L0 | `base-ubuntu` / `base-kylin` | 最小系统 + 国内源 + 证书 | amd64 + arm64 | 月度 |
| L1-a | `toolchain-cpp` | GCC/Clang/CMake/ninja | amd64 + arm64 | 按版本 |
| L1-b | `toolchain-gbench` | Google Benchmark + perf | amd64 + arm64 | 按版本 |
| L1-c | `toolchain-python` | Python + 常用包离线预置 | amd64 + arm64 | 按版本 |
| L1-d | `toolchain-common` | Git/zsh/tmux/ssh/vim | amd64 + arm64 | 月度 |
| L2-a | `services-docker` | Podman / Docker CE | amd64 + arm64 | 按版本 |
| L2-b | `services-ansible` | Ansible + Collection | amd64 + arm64 | 按版本 |
| L3 | `compose-full` / `compose-cpp` 等 | 面向场景组合 | amd64 + arm64 | 按需 |

**关键设计原则：**
- 所有外部依赖在构建时**离线预置**进镜像，目标机无需访问外网
- 每层通过 `FROM` 继承，变更只重建受影响的层及其上层
- 所有镜像同时构建 `amd64` + `arm64`，通过 `manifest list` 统一 tag

---

## 三、国内封锁规避策略

### 3.1 运行时规避

```
封锁困境                    规避方案
────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Docker Hub 被封           → 全部使用 GHCR / 阿里云ACR / 华为SWR
docker pull 超时          → OSS/OBS预置tar包，本地 docker load
Docker Desktop 限制       → 优先使用 Podman（无守护进程，无需root）
containerd 替代           → nerdctl + containerd 作为备选运行时
网络插件问题              → 镜像内置所有依赖，最小化运行时网络需求
```

### 3.2 构建时规避

```
问题场景                    规避方案
────────────────────────────────────────────────────
apt 源访问慢/失败         → L0 层统一替换为阿里云/华为云镜像源
pip 访问失败              → 配置 aliyun / tsinghua PyPI 镜像
GitHub Actions 构建       → 利用 GitHub 网络环境，无封锁困扰
国内CI平台降智            → 坚持使用 GitHub Actions，拒绝迁移
```

### 3.3 分发规避

```
问题场景                    规避方案
────────────────────────────────────────────────────
目标机无法访问GHCR        → OSS/OBS 存储 .tar.zst 包，内网HTTP分发
目标机无法访问外网        → 本地搭建简易 Registry（distribution镜像）
大文件传输                → 分层导出 + zstd 压缩，支持断点续传
```

---

## 四、构建能力设计

### 4.1 构建粒度（Makefile 入口）

```makefile
# 全量构建
make build-all

# 按层构建
make build LAYER=base
make build LAYER=toolchain
make build LAYER=services
make build LAYER=compose

# 单镜像构建

author: copilot
body:
Bootstraps a complete, runnable FastAPI auth backend for the SaaS accounting app — JWT register/login/protected routes, bcrypt hashing, Pydantic schemas, and a modular package layout that coexists with existing routes.

## New modules

- **`app/core/config.py`** — `Settings` class; reads `JWT_SECRET_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES` from `.env`
- **`app/core/security.py`** — `get_password_hash` / `verify_password` (bcrypt via passlib), `create_access_token` / `decode_access_token` (HS256 JWT via python-jose)
- **`app/models/user.py`** — `User` and `Company` SQLAlchemy models; `company_id` FK enables multi-tenant isolation
- **`app/schemas/user.py`** — `Token`, `TokenData`, `UserCreate`, `UserLogin`, `UserResponse`, `CompanyCreate/Response`
- **`app/routers/auth.py`** — `POST /api/auth/register`, `POST /api/auth/login`, `GET /api/auth/me`
- **`app/dependencies.py`** — `get_current_user` and `get_current_active_admin` dependency injection

## Package shadowing for backward compatibility

Creating `app/models/` and `app/schemas/` as packages shadows the flat `models.py`/`schemas.py` files. Their `__init__.py` files re-export all existing symbols so `from app import models, schemas` keeps working across all existing routes without modification.

## Bug fix: Conta self-referential relationship

The original `models.py` had an incorrect adjacency-list relationship that caused a SQLAlchemy mapper error on **every** database query (not just Conta queries). Fixed `remote_side` to the correct side:

```python
# Before (broken — same direction on both sides)
contas_filhas = relationship("Conta", remote_side=[conta_pai_id], backref="conta_pai")

# After (correct — remote_side on the many-to-one parent side)
contas_filhas = relationship("Conta", back_populates="conta_pai", foreign_keys=[conta_pai_id])
conta_pai     = relationship("Conta", back_populates="contas_filhas", remote_side=[id], foreign_keys=[conta_pai_id])
```

## Dependency

Added `python-jose[cryptography]==3.5.0` to `requirements.txt` (3.3.0 had a CVE for ECDSA algorithm confusion; 3.5.0 is clean).

- Provide at least one meta choice before the next cycle (e.g. intervention slot, stress bias, tick preset) and persist its effects into next-session initial conditions.

author: zingerlittlebee
body:
## Web Performance Audit — Fixes

Findings and fixes from a codebase audit of `dockerman.app` (Next.js 16 + Tailwind CSS v4 + Turbo).

### Fixes

**Critical: Image lazy-loading bug** (`SnapshotPlaygroundScroll.tsx`)
`loading={index >= 3 ? 'eager' : undefined}` should be `'lazy'`. This caused all 14 playground screenshots (~5.4MB of PNGs before optimizer compression) to download eagerly on page load. Only the first 3 are visible; the rest should be deferred.

**LCP image quality** (`HeroImage.tsx`)
Both hero images used `quality={100}`, the maximum. Changed to `quality={75}`, which is visually indistinguishable for UI screenshots but generates significantly smaller optimized images from Next.js's image pipeline.

**Render-blocking font** (`globals.css`)
`NanumPenScript` (a decorative handwriting font used for accent text) used `font-display: block`, which holds back text rendering until the font arrives. Changed to `font-display: swap` — text renders immediately with a fallback and swaps when the font loads.

**797 KB GIF eagerly downloaded on CSS parse** (`globals.css`)
`/images/i-love-you-love.gif` was referenced as a CSS `mask` fallback in `::view-transition-new(root)`. Browsers pre-fetch URLs in CSS at parse time — before any user interaction. The GIF is only needed for the theme-toggle animation (which already sets `--transition-mask` via JS). Changed the fallback from the URL to `none` to defer the fetch until the user actually clicks the toggle.

**Long-term caching for static assets** (`next.config.mjs`)
Added `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` for `/screenshots/*`, `/fonts/*`, and `/images/*`. Previously these served with `max-age=0, must-revalidate`, forcing a conditional re-fetch on every page visit.

**Removed unused dependency**
`@tabler/icons-react` was listed in `package.json` but is never imported anywhere in the codebase.

### Not changed (informational)

- **Redirect on first visit** (`/` → `/en`): The middleware handles this at the edge and sets a 1-year cookie, so only the very first visit incurs the redirect hop. Acceptable tradeoff for i18n.
- **Dual animation libraries (GSAP + Motion)**: Both are legitimately used — GSAP for scroll-triggered animations via Lenis, Motion for component-level transitions. Consolidating would be a larger refactor.
- **90 KB HTML, uncompressed in headers**: Vercel handles Brotli transparently for browser requests; the `curl -sI` probe didn't advertise `Accept-Encoding: br` correctly.

### Motivation
- Beam drawing commands were being injected in the `OnPlayDrawBegin` phase and later overwritten when the Play draw lists were rebuilt, causing Beamos beam visuals to not appear. 
- The code treated `gBeamosLaserDL` as a segmented/relocated asset and attempted to load/validate it via `ResourceMgr_LoadGfxByName`, which is unnecessary in SoH where the DL is a host pointer.

### Description
- Moved beam display-list injection from the `OnPlayDrawBegin` hook into the existing `OnPlayDrawEnd` hook so beam draw commands are appended after scene DLs are built and before `RangedFuseMenu::Draw` by calling `Fuse_DrawRangedBeamEmitters_Hook` and committing `play->state.gfxCtx->polyOpa.p`/`polyXlu.p` there. 
- Preserved the same capture/commit pattern and the rate-limited `[FuseDBG] BeamDrawCommit: opaDelta=... xluDelta=...` logging used when committing the poly pointers. 
- Simplified beam DL usage inside `Fuse_DrawRangedBeamEmitters` to call `gSPDisplayList(p++, gBeamosLaserDL);` directly and removed the `ResourceMgr_LoadGfxByName` / lazy `laserDl` lookup and its null-DL fallback, aligning the code with SoH’s host-pointer model for `gBeamosLaserDL`. 
- Removed the now-unused `ResourceManagerHelpers` include and the `sLastBeamDrawNullDlLogFrame` state while preserving existing `[FuseDBG]` logging such as `BeamDraw`, `BeamDrawSkip`, and `BeamDrawAppend` and adding the retained rate-limited commit log.

author: ml12580
body:
…found (#7631)

On Windows, Node.js 18.20.2+ rejects spawning .cmd/.bat files directly without shell, causing EINVAL errors. The existing code attempted to resolve npm/npx to node.exe + npm-cli.js, but this fails when npm-cli.js is not found (e.g., with nvm-windows or portable Node installations).

This fix adds npm and npx to the cmdCommands list, ensuring they get the .cmd suffix when resolveNpmArgvForWindows returns null. The .cmd files are then properly wrapped via cmd.exe /d /s /c for safe execution.

Closes #7631

## Summary

- **Problem**: On Windows, `openclaw plugins install` fails with `Error: spawn EINVAL` when the npm-cli.js file is not found in the Node.js installation directory (common with nvm-windows, portable Node, or non-standard installations).
- **Why it matters**: This blocks Windows users from installing plugins, a core functionality of OpenClaw.
- **What changed**: Added `npm` and `npx` to the `cmdCommands` list in `resolveCommand()`, ensuring they get the `.cmd` suffix when `resolveNpmArgvForWindows()` fails. The resulting `.cmd` files are then properly wrapped via `cmd.exe /d /s /c` for safe execution.
- **What did NOT change**: The preferred path (using `node.exe + npm-cli.js`) remains unchanged. This fix only affects the fallback behavior when npm-cli.js is not found.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #7631

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Windows users can now successfully run `openclaw plugins install <package>` even when their Node.js installation doesn't have npm-cli.js in the expected location.
- No configuration changes required.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`No`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No` - uses existing cmd.exe wrapper with proper escaping)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Windows 10/11
- Runtime: Node.js v22.x (installed via nvm-windows or portable)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: N/A
- Relevant config: Default OpenClaw installation

### Steps

1. Install Node.js via nvm-windows or as a portable installation
2. Run `npm install -g openclaw`
3. Execute `openclaw plugins install @m1heng-clawd/feishu`

### Expected

- Plugin downloads and installs successfully

### Actual (before fix)

- Error: `spawn EINVAL` at `runCommandWithTimeout`

### Actual (after fix)

- Plugin downloads and installs successfully (either via node.exe + npm-cli.js or via npm.cmd fallback)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- Test added: `wraps npm.cmd via cmd.exe when npm-cli.js is not found` in `src/process/exec.windows.test.ts`

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios:
  - All existing tests pass (`pnpm check`, `pnpm vitest run src/process/exec.test.ts src/process/exec.windows.test.ts`)
  - New test covers both code paths (node.exe + npm-cli.js preferred, npm.cmd fallback)
- Edge cases checked:
  - Behavior unchanged for non-Windows platforms
  - Behavior unchanged when npm-cli.js exists
  - Fallback correctly wraps npm.cmd via cmd.exe
- What you did **not** verify:
  - Manual testing on a Windows machine without npm-cli.js (would require specific Node.js installation)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert commit or use previous version
- Files/config to restore: None
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: None expected - this is a fallback fix

## Risks and Mitigations

1. **Risk**: The cmd.exe wrapper might behave differently than direct npm-cli.js execution
   - **Mitigation**: The existing code already uses this pattern for pnpm/yarn; npm/npx follow the same proven approach

2. **Risk**: Some Windows environments might not have npm.cmd in PATH
   - **Mitigation**: This was already a failure case; the fix doesn't make it worse, and the original error message would still appear

author: juniyadi
body:
This pull request refactors the contact import process to use a queued job for handling CSV uploads, improving scalability and reliability. The import logic is moved from the Livewire component to a new `ImportContactsFromCsv` job class, and related helpers are extracted for better separation of concerns. Tests are updated to verify that the import job is correctly queued.

**Contact import process refactor:**

* Added the `ImportContactsFromCsv` job class to encapsulate the contact import logic, moving file reading and processing out of the Livewire component. (`app/Jobs/ImportContactsFromCsv.php`)
* Updated the Livewire component (`pages::contacts.index`) to queue the import job after file upload, removing all inline CSV parsing and contact creation logic. (`resources/views/pages/contacts/⚡index.blade.php`)
* Extracted the CSV import logic into a new service class, `CsvContactImporter`, for reusable and testable contact import functionality. (`app/Support/Contacts/CsvContactImporter.php`)

**CSV file reading improvements:**

* Refactored `CsvUploadedFileReader` to add a new static method `readRowsFromContents`, separating file reading from content parsing for more flexible usage. (`app/Support/CsvUploadedFileReader.php`)

**Testing and queueing:**

* Updated and added feature tests to ensure the import job is queued after a CSV upload and that queue configuration is properly set for test isolation. (`tests/Feature/ContactsManagementTest.php`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7c547b2cd5bc42a3dfe57bef69ecdfef68836377df3a651ff8fc14bb4298dd93R3-R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7c547b2cd5bc42a3dfe57bef69ecdfef68836377df3a651ff8fc14bb4298dd93R263-R279)

These changes make the contact import process asynchronous, more maintainable, and ready for larger CSV files or future enhancements.

author: gunnargray-dev
body:
## What

Adds 7 new backend modules (trends, categories, badges, digest, compare, API, CLI) plus `run_batch_analysis()` in the pipeline. This is the full Phase 1+3+4 backend.

## Why

Completes the analytical and operational surface area needed to query the leaderboard in every meaningful way: trends over time, head-to-head comparisons, badge URLs for READMEs, weekly digests, and a fully typed JSON API layer that a future web server can call without touching SQLite directly.

## How

**New modules:**
- `src/trends.py` — score delta, rank history, biggest movers/fallers, weekly aggregation by ISO week
- `src/categories.py` — keyword-based category detection with topic-weighted confidence scoring (24 categories)
- `src/badges.py` — shields.io badge URL generation for overall score, grade, trend arrow, and category
- `src/digest.py` — Markdown session digest: new projects, top 10, movers, grade distribution, aggregate stats
- `src/compare.py` — head-to-head comparison with per-dimension results (overall, health, complexity, security, dead_code), winner logic, `.to_dict()` and `.to_markdown()` output
- `src/api.py` — pure-function JSON API: `get_leaderboard_json`, `get_project_json`, `get_trends_json`, `get_comparison_json`, `get_categories_json`, `get_stats_json`, `get_digest_json`
- `src/cli.py` — argparse CLI: `top`, `detail`, `refresh`, `refresh-all`, `seed`, `trends`, `categories`, `stats`, `compare`, `digest`, `badge`

**Updates:**
- `src/pipeline.py` — `run_batch_analysis(db_path, session, token=None)` re-analyzes all tracked projects
- `src/models.py` — fix `sort_by="stars"` in `get_leaderboard()` (was doing `ORDER BY r.stars`, stars lives in `projects` table)

## Tests

236 tests pass. 7 new test modules covering all new code.

```
236 passed in 0.47s
```

## Tweet

Just shipped the full analytics backend for Awake Leaderboard: trend tracking, head-to-head comparisons, shields.io badges, weekly digests, and a CLI you can actually use. Pure Python, zero deps, 236 tests. 🐍📊 #buildinpublic

body:
This pull request primarily updates and expands the test coverage for WAV file reading and writing, with a focus on normalization behavior and input flexibility. It also refactors the usage of the `read_wav` function throughout the codebase to consistently use the `ChannelFrame.read_wav` class method, and exposes this method as the public `read_wav` API. Additionally, it introduces improvements to the handling of input types and normalization options in both the code and tests.

Key changes include:

**Test Enhancements and Normalization Handling:**

* Added comprehensive tests in `tests/frames/test_channel_frame.py` and `tests/io/test_wav_io.py` to verify the behavior of reading WAV files with and without normalization, including for int16 data, float32 data, file paths, byte streams, and non-seekable streams. These tests ensure that the `normalize` argument works as expected and that various input types are supported. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c513a56441c3bc39fbafe2054ca40aa55afc59cff55d6fc5ecee801900de32c3R1542-R1592) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c513a56441c3bc39fbafe2054ca40aa55afc59cff55d6fc5ecee801900de32c3L1553-R1641) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3a59d44deff0225d4f01b7f020d63f1c7d49c6dc1e15371c8c487a43f8436745L132-R225) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-3a59d44deff0225d4f01b7f020d63f1c7d49c6dc1e15371c8c487a43f8436745L203-R273)
* Updated tests in `tests/io/test_file_readers.py` to always pass `normalize=True` when reading data, ensuring that test expectations match the new normalization logic. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5db446db7271e075d4547aca5d2868ca7e36762d2bffc9a307967bdc2527a2fbL54-R66) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5db446db7271e075d4547aca5d2868ca7e36762d2bffc9a307967bdc2527a2fbR80) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5db446db7271e075d4547aca5d2868ca7e36762d2bffc9a307967bdc2527a2fbL85-R100) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-5db446db7271e075d4547aca5d2868ca7e36762d2bffc9a307967bdc2527a2fbL106-R115) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-5db446db7271e075d4547aca5d2868ca7e36762d2bffc9a307967bdc2527a2fbL115-R126)

**API and Codebase Refactoring:**

* Refactored all usages of the legacy `read_wav` function to use `ChannelFrame.read_wav` directly, both in the test suite and in the public API exposed in `wandas/__init__.py`. This unifies the WAV reading interface and ensures consistent behavior. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3a59d44deff0225d4f01b7f020d63f1c7d49c6dc1e15371c8c487a43f8436745L41-R41) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3a59d44deff0225d4f01b7f020d63f1c7d49c6dc1e15371c8c487a43f8436745L91-R91) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3a59d44deff0225d4f01b7f020d63f1c7d49c6dc1e15371c8c487a43f8436745L107-R107) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-3a59d44deff0225d4f01b7f020d63f1c7d49c6dc1e15371c8c487a43f8436745L132-R225) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-3a59d44deff0225d4f01b7f020d63f1c7d49c6dc1e15371c8c487a43f8436745L260-R303) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-ba85231f18f853fcc1d24365e1e8a79820e62b2325eed52777ca1879e6ef204fL8-R14)
* Updated the `ChannelFrame.from_file` method signature to include a `normalize` argument, allowing callers to control normalization directly when creating a `ChannelFrame` from a file.

**Additional Improvements:**

* Added a test to verify that writing float32 data with values in [-1, 1] uses the correct "FLOAT" subtype in the WAV file output.
* Improved error handling in tests to accept both `FileNotFoundError` and `RuntimeError` when files are missing.

author: alex-solovyev
body:
## Summary

- Rewrites the pulse external-contributor idempotency guard to **fail closed** on API errors, preventing duplicate comments
- Separates exit code checking from output parsing so API failures are detected reliably
- Applies the same fix to the permission-failure comment guard

## Root Cause

The previous fix (#2796) changed `2>/dev/null` to `2>&1` on the label check, but this made API error text flow into the `$labels` variable. Since error messages don't match `^external-contributor$`, the `if/elif/else` chain fell through to the `else` branch (post comment) on every pulse cycle. PR #2792 accumulated 20+ identical comments.

## What Changed

**Before:** Single `if/elif/else` chain where API errors in either check caused fall-through to posting.

**After:** Three-step approach:
1. Check label (capture exit code separately via `$?`)
2. Check comment (capture exit code separately via `$?`)
3. Three-way decision:
   - Either API call failed → **skip posting** (fail closed, next pulse retries)
   - Label OR comment already exists → skip (re-add label if missing)
   - Both succeeded AND neither exists → safe to post

Same pattern applied to the permission-failure comment guard (outcome 3 in the external contributor gate).

## Testing

- Markdown lint: 0 errors
- Logic trace: API error → `label_exit != 0` → first branch → skip posting (correct)
- Logic trace: label exists → `has_label=true` → second branch → skip posting (correct)
- Logic trace: comment exists → `has_comment=true` → second branch → skip posting (correct)
- Logic trace: both succeed, neither exists → third branch → post (correct)

author: vinaysagargonabavi
body:
## What is the purpose of the change
This is a v2 approach following feedback on PR #4280 — schema evolution responsibility stays in `SchemaCoordinator` rather than adding state to `PostTransformOperator`, keeping the transform operator stateless as intended by PR #4056.

When a Flink CDC pipeline uses transform projections and the pipeline is restarted from a savepoint/checkpoint with an updated projection, the downstream sink never receives schema change events for the new/removed columns, leaving the sink schema stale and out of sync with the actual projected data.

This PR fixes the issue by teaching SchemaCoordinator to detect schema differences when a `CreateTableEvent` arrives for an already-known table. Instead of treating it as redundant, the coordinator computes the schema diff and emits appropriate `AddColumnEvent`/`DropColumnEvent`/`AlterColumnTypeEvent` downstream. `PostTransformOperator` remains stateless - it's a pure mapping node.

## Brief change log

- `SchemaUtils.isSchemaChangeEventRedundant()`: CreateTableEvent is now redundant only if the table exists AND the schema is identical (was: just existence check)
- `SchemaCoordinator.deduceEvolvedSchemaChanges()`: When a CreateTableEvent arrives for an existing table in 1:1 routing, computes schema diff via SchemaMergingUtils.getSchemaDifference() and returns diff events instead of forwarding the raw CreateTableEvent

**Note**: `isSchemaChangeEventRedundant` is also called by Hudi and Paimon sink connectors. The behavioral change is a bugfix for those paths as well (they were silently dropping CreateTableEvents with changed schemas), but no connector-specific code was modified.

## Verifying this change
3 new test methods across 3 files:

- `SchemaUtilsTest`: Redundancy checks for CreateTableEvent - non-existent table, same schema, extra columns, type diff, fewer columns
- `SchemaMergingUtilsTest`: Diff scenarios for projection changes - add column, drop column, type change, swap columns, identical schemas
- `SchemaEvolveTest`: End-to-end through SchemaOperator + SchemaCoordinator - add column, drop column, type change, identical schema (no-op)

## Does this pull request potentially affect one of the following parts

- Dependencies: no
- The public API: no
- The runtime per-record code path: no (only affects schema change event processing)
- Anything that affects deployment or recovery: yes (changes how CreateTableEvent is handled after checkpoint restore)

## Documentation

- Does this pull request introduce a new feature? No (fixes existing behavior gap)

author: jeffreypalermo
body:
Closes #676

We have a growing number of acceptance tests that use playwright in order to open up a browser and use the application but the browser closes and we have no idea what the final screen looked like before we close the browser we need an automated way to capture a final screenshot before each acceptance test ends if we can find a way to do the screen shot right before closing the browser Then we can get a good picture of what the screen looks like when the test is performing its assertions. This should be automatic across the test suite and should not be an extra line of code that every test has to declare I believe that we can do it right before the code that closes the web browser Each of these screenshots need to be saved in the proper according to the in unit framework and exported so that when in Github Actions we can see the screenshots along with the test reports automatically

The issue is about creating an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server - this is a backend-only, programmatic protocol for AI agents. There is no user-facing UI in this feature.

## User Experience Design

**User Flow:**
N/A - This feature creates an MCP server for programmatic AI agent access via stdio transport. There is no user-facing interface; AI clients (Claude, Copilot, Cursor) connect programmatically to the server process. Users interact with the work order system through their existing AI assistant interfaces, not through any new UI components in this application.

**UI Components:**
- New: N/A - No new UI components; MCP server is a headless backend process
- Modified: N/A - No existing components are modified

**Error States:**
- MCP tool precondition failures (e.g., invalid state transition): Return structured error message in MCP tool response JSON, surfaced by the AI client in its chat interface
- Database connection failure: MCP server process exits with error code; AI client reports tool unavailable
- Invalid parameters (e.g., non-existent work order number): Return descriptive error string in tool response

**Accessibility:**
- N/A - No UI components; accessibility is handled by the AI client applications (Claude, Copilot, Cursor) that consume this MCP server
- N/A - Screen reader and keyboard navigation concerns are delegated to the consuming AI client interfaces

## Technical Design

**Affected Components:**

| Layer | File | Action |
|-------|------|--------|
| Test Infrastructure | `src/AcceptanceTests/AcceptanceTestBase.cs` | Modify |

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Modify `src/AcceptanceTests/AcceptanceTestBase.cs` - Add automatic final screenshot capture in the `TearDownAsync` method before closing the browser. The screenshot should be taken after tracing stops but before `Page.CloseAsync()` is called. The screenshot filename should follow the pattern `{ClassName}-{TestName}-final-{TestId}.png` for uniqueness.
2. Modify `src/AcceptanceTests/AcceptanceTestBase.cs` - Store the final screenshot in a dedicated `final-screenshots` subdirectory under `TestContext.CurrentContext.WorkDirectory` to organize outputs alongside the existing `playwright-traces` folder.
3. Modify `src/AcceptanceTests/AcceptanceTestBase.cs` - Register the final screenshot as a test attachment using `TestContext.AddTestAttachment()` so NUnit includes it in test reports and GitHub Actions can surface it in test result artifacts.
4. Modify `src/AcceptanceTests/AcceptanceTestBase.cs` - Ensure the final screenshot is captured regardless of test outcome (pass, fail, skip) by wrapping the screenshot logic in its own try-catch block to prevent failures from affecting other teardown operations.
5. Modify `src/AcceptanceTests/AcceptanceTestBase.cs` - Ensure directory creation (`Directory.CreateDirectory`) before saving screenshots to handle parallel test execution where the directory may not exist yet.

**Dependencies:** None

**Database Migrations:** None

**Tests:**

| Type | Location | Coverage |
|------|----------|----------|
| Unit | N/A | No unit tests required - this is test infrastructure that will be validated by running the acceptance test suite itself |
| Integration | N/A | No integration tests required |
| Acceptance | `src/AcceptanceTests/` | Validation by running any existing acceptance test and verifying: (1) final screenshot PNG file exists in `final-screenshots` directory, (2) screenshot is attached to NUnit test results |

Based on the issue analysis, this is a test infrastructure change that modifies `AcceptanceTestBase.cs` to automatically capture final screenshots before closing the browser. The technical design explicitly states validation is performed by running existing acceptance tests and verifying screenshot files exist.

## Test Design

**Acceptance Tests:** None required

**Rationale:** Backend-only change - This is test infrastructure code that modifies the `AcceptanceTestBase.cs` teardown logic. Per the technical design, validation is performed by running any existing acceptance test and verifying: (1) final screenshot PNG file exists in `final-screenshots` directory, (2) screenshot is attached to NUnit test results. No new acceptance test scenarios are needed; the existing test suite serves as validation.

body:
## Objetivo
Este PR introduz uma reformulação visual completa da Landing Page sob a estética Frutiger Aero (anos 2000) e implementa o grande trunfo arquitetural do projeto: O Intelligent Feed Canvas. Além do visual nostálgico e responsivo, a física do Canvas foi reescrita utilizando matemática nodal para gerar "Ilhas Temáticas", agrupando semânticamente conexões de dados processadas pelo backend em PgVector.

## Principais Funcionalidades Implementadas

### 1. Frutiger Aero Experiência (Frontend UI/UX)
- Reformulação total de cores globais com tons ricos cianos, azuis vibrantes e verdes limão (`index.css` Tailwind themes).
- Componentes 100% Glassmorphism (Vidro fosco) usando mix de `backdrop-blur` avançado, brilhos especulares (box-shadows duplos) e transparências acrílicas (`AeroModal`, [GelButton](cci:1://file:///home/epaim/graphcognitio-web/src/components/ui/GelButton.tsx:13:0-27:1)).
- Cursor Trail interativo e suave com micro-partículas (brilhos rosa choque) e background dinâmico com orbs de luz em movimento (`BubbleLayer.tsx`).
- Refinamento tipográfico e layout assimétrico moderno priorizando a estética expansiva.

### 2. Intelligent Topic Clustering (Feed Canvas)
- Implementação física de Sub-Espirais Nódicas: O Feed infinito ([FeedCanvas.tsx](cci:7://file:///home/epaim/graphcognitio-web/src/features/feed/components/FeedCanvas.tsx:0:0-0:0)) agora interpreta o array de [topicKeywords](cci:1://file:///home/epaim/graphcognitio/src/main/java/io/github/eduardopaim/graphcognitio/posts/service/PostService.java:434:4-436:5) que chega da API Spring Boot.
- Formação de Ilhas Temáticas: Reescrita da física de coordenadas em [worldPlacement.ts](cci:7://file:///home/epaim/graphcognitio-web/src/features/feed/canvas/worldPlacement.ts:0:0-0:0). O algoritmo detecta a similaridade dos posts (interseção de assuntos) e os atrai gravitacionalmente para uma mesma "Âncora" principal. 
- Espaçamento Matemático Misto: A distância das categorias distintas (Ex: "React" x "Spring Boot") foi aumentada colossalmente (`BASE_RADIUS * 4.2`), enquanto os "filhotes" do mesmo tema ganharam uma Constante de Atração altíssima (`SUB_RADIUS * 0.15`), montando aglomerados e grids perfeitamente encaixados que nascem ao renderizar.
- Canvas Core: Criação do marcador central visual para referenciar o eixo [(0,0)](cci:1://file:///home/epaim/graphcognitio/src/main/java/io/github/eduardopaim/graphcognitio/posts/service/FeedContextService.java:121:8-123:9) com botões robustos de navegação e controle de zoom desbloqueado para visualização "God Mode" (macro).

### 3. Qualidade & Testes (Vitest)
- Incorporação da suíte de testes unitários super-rápidos do Vitest.
- Adição da file de validação física [worldPlacement.test.ts](cci:7://file:///home/epaim/graphcognitio-web/src/features/feed/canvas/worldPlacement.test.ts:0:0-0:0) garantindo com cálculos de Distância Euclidiana e Assertions matemáticas exatas que posts isolados estão longes entre si, enquanto posts de mesmos assuntos caem juntos no raio máximo permitido do nódulo, blindando a funcionalidade complexa.

## Checklist de Revisão
- [x] Testes Unitários criados/atualizados e passando (Vitest).
- [x] Validação lógica de dependências `useEffect` e React Query no modo Infinito (Feed limitation).
- [x] O código está limpo, componentes refatorados e removidos imports obsoletos.
- [x] Design verificado em resoluções Web Convencionais.

body:
## Summary
This PR enhances location handling by adding support for resolving Google Maps short URLs (maps.app.goo.gl and goo.gl/maps) to extract coordinates, and improves text-based geocoding with regional context hints.

## Key Changes

- **New `resolveShortMapsUrl()` function** in `geo.ts`: Resolves Google Maps short URLs by following HTTP redirects with a 5-second timeout. Returns the full URL or null if resolution fails or the URL is not a short Maps URL.

- **Short URL resolution in event processing**: Updated `resolveCoords()` in `merge.ts` to attempt resolving short Maps URLs before falling back to text-based geocoding, enabling coordinate extraction from shortened links.

- **Region hint support in `EventLocationMap`**: Added optional `regionHint` prop to disambiguate text-based geocoding. When coordinates are unavailable and a region hint is provided, it's appended to the location name for more accurate Maps searches (e.g., "Bar Name, New York City, NY").

- **Region hint propagation**: Updated `EventDetailPage` and `EventDetailPanel` to pass the kennel's region as a hint to the map component.

- **Comprehensive test coverage**: Added 8 test cases for `resolveShortMapsUrl()` covering success cases (maps.app.goo.gl and goo.gl/maps), validation (non-short URLs, empty strings), error handling (network failures, timeouts), and edge cases (no redirect, non-maps goo.gl URLs).

## Implementation Details

- The `resolveShortMapsUrl()` function uses a HEAD request with `redirect: "follow"` to efficiently follow redirects without downloading response bodies
- Includes a 5-second timeout via AbortController to prevent hanging on unresponsive servers
- All errors (network, timeout, invalid URLs) are caught and return null gracefully
- Region hint is only appended when needed (no coordinates, hint not already in location name) to avoid redundancy

author: segin
body:
💡 **What:** 
Implemented a small inline directory entry cache (`dcache`) inside `ext2_node_t`. It caches up to 16 recently looked up `(name, name_len, inode_num)` pairs to avoid repetitive linear block searches during `ext2_finddir`. Filenames exceeding 63 characters safely bypass the cache to prevent truncation and false-positive hits. Invalidation logic is wired up to `ext2_remove_entry`.

🎯 **Why:** 
EXT2 traditionally implements directory lookups as a linear scan across data blocks, which becomes noticeably slow as directory entries grow or for repeated access to the same file. Adding a dcache short-circuits this traversal logic, significantly improving file access performance.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** 
A standalone performance test (`tests/sys/test_ext2_finddir_dcache_perf.c`) was built to simulate 10,000 repetitive lookups of a target file located at the end of a directory containing 1000 entries.

*   **Baseline (Linear Search):** ~0.434341 seconds
*   **Optimized (Dcache hit):** ~0.001038 seconds
*   **Improvement:** ~99.76%

### Motivation

- Admin was sending raw/unqualified filter fragments to PostgREST which caused parse errors like `PGRST100` when URL params (e.g. `provincia`) were passed directly into queries. 
- Filters from the URL must be decoded, trimmed, and ignored if empty, and the data layer must emit valid PostgREST operators (`eq`, `ilike`, `or(...)`) rather than raw `key=value` fragments.

### Description

- Added a new helper `buildAdminFilters` at `app/admin/build-admin-filters.ts` which trims, `decodeURIComponent`-s (with fallback), lowercases the search `q`, and ignores empty values.
- Updated `app/admin/page.tsx` to use `buildAdminFilters()` and pass structured filters into the data layer instead of building raw query fragments or doing full client-side filtering after loading everything.
- Refactored `listPeople` and `listEvents` in `lib/data.ts` to accept filter options and to build PostgREST-compatible query strings using an `appendQuery` helper that emits `eq` and `ilike` operators and URL-encodes values; people search uses `or=(full_name.ilike...,stage_name.ilike...)` and events use `name=ilike...`.
- Removed the previous in-memory `filteredPeople`/`filteredEvents` post-fetch filtering paths so results are pre-filtered by Supabase where possible.

author: lvy-lip
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a Chiikawa-style couple growth experience with four main tabs (Home / Study / Emotion / Shop) to manage shared todos, emotion logs, points and shop items in a minimal-intrusion way. 
- Use cloud database and cloud functions to centralize business logic for points settlement, record storage and purchases while keeping couple binding simple (`defaultCoupleId`) for initial usage.

### Description
- Reworked app-level configuration and styling by updating `miniprogram/app.json`, adding Chiikawa pastel theme styles in `miniprogram/app.wxss`, and adding `defaultCoupleId` + collection map in `miniprogram/app.js`.
- Added four pages under `miniprogram/pages/`: `Home` (swiper banners, last 7-day study stats, points), `Study` (add/edit/delete todos, daily/today types, completion flow), `Emotion` (text + multi-image upload with cloud `fileID` storage and timeline view) and `Shop` (product list, points display, purchase flow).
- Implemented cloud functions to handle core operations: `getHomeStats` (dashboard and banners), `settleTodoComplete` (one-time points settlement using `settled` flag), `saveEmotionRecord` (persist emotion entries with images), and `purchaseProduct` (points validation, deduction, stock decrement and order creation).
- Kept changes minimal-intrusion by leaving legacy files in repo and using a simple `solo-default-couple` mode for couple binding so the new flow can run immediately and be extended later.

### Testing
- Ran syntax checks with `node --check` for the new cloud functions and page scripts (checked `getHomeStats`, `settleTodoComplete`, `saveEmotionRecord`, `purchaseProduct` and the four page JS files) and they succeeded. 
- Performed local validation of page/cloud-function wiring by calling `getHomeStats` and other calls from page code paths in development (JS checks), and default product creation logic is included when no products exist. 
- Attempted automated screenshot with Playwright (`mcp__browser_tools__run_playwright_script`) failed because there is no HTTP-served web preview for a WeChat mini program in this environment, which does not affect WeChat runtime behavior.

Implemented a performance optimization for the `get_recent_sessions` query in `core/infra/cloud/firebase/queries.py`. Also performed a comprehensive project-wide linting and formatting cleanup to resolve CI failures.

- **Baseline (Original):** ~101ms

author: jlowhy
body:
## What was changed
This updates local dev infra behavior so `pnpm dev` restarts preserve Postgres state and documents reset semantics explicitly. It also makes teardown commands (`pnpm dev:down`, `pnpm dev:reset`, `pnpm dev:reset:hard`) independent from tunnel-only env interpolation by making tunnel compose interpolation non-fatal during teardown, while keeping startup fail-fast in `scripts/dev/start.ts`.

- `infra/local/docker-compose.yml`: changed Postgres named-volume mount target from `/var/lib/postgresql/data` to `/var/lib/postgresql` so Postgres 18 (`PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/18/docker`) writes to the persistent named volume.
- `infra/local/docker-compose.yml`: changed tunnel interpolation from required forms to defaults:
  - `CLOUDFLARED_CONFIG_PATH` now defaults to `./.generated/cloudflared-config.yml`
  - `CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN` now defaults to empty string
  This allows `docker compose down` to parse the file without tunnel env.
- `README.md`: documented `pnpm dev:reset` and `pnpm dev:reset:hard` and added a behavior summary for `dev`, `dev:down`, `dev:reset`, and `dev:reset:hard`.
- **Compatibility note**: this changes on-volume Postgres layout for existing local named volumes. Existing developer volumes created with the old mount path will not be reused as-is and require a one-time local reset/migration.

## How to review
Entrypoints first:
- `infra/local/docker-compose.yml`
- `README.md`

Suggested review order:
1. Inspect `infra/local/docker-compose.yml` Postgres mount change and verify it matches Postgres 18 `PGDATA` behavior.
2. Inspect `infra/local/docker-compose.yml` tunnel interpolation defaults and confirm this unblocks `docker compose down` without tunnel env while startup validation remains in `scripts/dev/start.ts`.
3. Read `README.md` updates for reset semantics and ensure wording matches implemented behavior.
4. Validate locally with commands below.

Local validation commands:
- `pnpm dev:reset`
- `pnpm dev` (create data), stop, `pnpm dev` again, verify data persists
- `pnpm dev:reset` then verify data is wiped

## What the implication was
`pnpm dev` now behaves as level-1 teardown semantics (containers/network recycled; volumes persist). Reset commands remain explicit destructive paths.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[pnpm dev start] --> B[compose up infra]
  B --> C[app startup + migrations]
  C --> D[pnpm dev stop]
  D --> E[compose down --remove-orphans]
  E --> F[Named volumes preserved]

  G[pnpm dev:reset] --> H[compose down --remove-orphans --volumes]
  H --> I[Postgres + registry volumes removed]

  J[pnpm dev:reset:hard] --> K[compose down --remove-orphans --volumes --rmi local]
  K --> L[Volumes removed + local compose images removed]
```

Implications:
- Positive: DB state persists across normal `pnpm dev` restart cycles.
- Positive: teardown commands no longer fail when tunnel env vars are absent.
- Tradeoff: existing local Postgres named volumes from the old mount path require one-time reset/migration to align with new layout.

## Checks and tests performed
- `pnpm format`
  - What: repository formatting
  - Expected outcome: no formatting failures
  - How: ran root formatter script
- `pnpm lint`
  - What: repo lint checks
  - Expected outcome: no lint violations
  - How: ran root lint script (`turbo run lint`)
- `pnpm typecheck`
  - What: repository type checking
  - Expected outcome: no type errors
  - How: ran root typecheck script (`turbo run typecheck` + scripts typecheck)
- `pnpm test`
  - What: repository test suites
  - Expected outcome: passing tests
  - How: ran root test script (`turbo run test`)
- Manual case 1: `pnpm dev:reset` with tunnel env vars unset
  - What: teardown behavior without tunnel env
  - Expected outcome: reset succeeds without interpolation error
  - How: executed `unset CLOUDFLARED_CONFIG_PATH CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN ...; pnpm dev:reset`
- Manual case 2: Postgres persistence across `compose down` (no volumes)
  - What: level-1 persistence behavior
  - Expected outcome: inserted probe row remains after down/up cycle without `--volumes`
  - How: start postgres, create probe table/row, `compose down --remove-orphans`, start again, query probe row

No property-based tests were added or changed.

## Summary
Added a new `RemoveAssignFromAST` AST transformer class to remove assignment statements from configuration file ASTs, specifically designed to strip `_base_` variable assignments before config compilation.

## Changes
- **New `RemoveAssignFromAST` class**: An `ast.NodeTransformer` subclass that removes assignment statements matching a specified target name
  - Takes a `key` parameter (e.g., `'_base_'`) to identify which assignments to remove
  - Implements `visit_Assign()` method to filter out matching assignments by returning `None`
  - Prevents the specified key from appearing in the resulting config dictionary after code execution
  - Includes comprehensive docstring explaining its purpose and usage

## Implementation Details
- The transformer checks if an assignment's first target is an `ast.Name` node with an `id` matching the configured key
- Returns `None` to remove matching nodes from the AST, while passing through all other assignment statements unchanged
- Positioned before the existing `ImportTransformer` class in the module
